title: Probe-run: queue slices & latency spectra (WIP)
content:
Status: WIP - exploratory probing of queue-slice (slice = contiguous set of inflight requests compacted into a scheduling unit) heuristics and their effect on latency spectra and fairness. Intention: find knobs that reduce p99/p999 tail without regressing p50/p95 and preserve proportional fairness across customers/workloads.

Background/context:
- We introduced "queue slices" in the runtime as a mid-granularity scheduling primitive to group compatible requests for batching. Current default: fixed-max-slice-size=32, slice-timeout-ms=18, no slice-preemption.
- Observed symptom: occasional multi-100ms tail events during sustained medium burst (60-120 RPS) for long-context models (8k seq). Microburst analysis suggests slice formation + KV cache misses amplify latency.

Goals for this doc:
1) Profile where slice-related latency accrues (queueing vs assembly vs kernel startup vs kv-cache fetch).
2) Evaluate slice-sizing heuristics: fixed-size, adaptive-by-occupancy, quantile-based compaction.
3) Measure fairness: variance in per-customer p99 under mixed workloads.
4) Produce a candidate knob set for canary rollout.

Quick notes on measurements and infra:
- Testbed: 4x A100-40GB serving nodes, model: open-llama-13B with KV-cache enabled, sequence length 8192, typical request prompt length 350 tokens.
- Workloads: mix A (steady 80 RPS single-tenant), mix B (10 tenants, Poisson arrivals mean 40 RPS combined), spike-run: sinusoidal 0->200 RPS every 120s.
- Metrics captured: request enqueue timestamp, slice-formed timestamp, batch-dispatched timestamp, kernel-start, kernel-end, kv-cache-hit boolean, tokens-generated, latency per-stage.
- Trace sampling: 1 in 50 full traces; aggregated histograms for every tenant.
- Tools: runtime tracing (zipkin-like), perf counters, eBPF-based kernel overhead probe, custom histograms exported to OTLP.

Experiment matrix (high-level):
- Slice size policy: fixed(8/16/32), adaptive(max 64 shrink-to-16), quantile-target(90th-packing), small-first (prefer small requests to avoid head-of-line blocking).
- Timeout-ms: 6, 12, 18, 30.
- Preemption: off, soft (can preempt if waiting > 2x mean-assembly-time), hard (preempt older slices when new high-priority requests arrive).
- Fairness modes: round-robin slice selection, proportional (weight by tenant SLA), latency-priority (prioritize oldest waiting).

Representative results (raw excerpts):
- Fixed-32 / timeout-18 / preempt-off / RR:
  p50=22ms p95=58ms p99=214ms p999=780ms
  KV-hit-rate=78% overall
  notes: tail dominated by slices that waited for full-size fill during intermittent bursts; kernel start variance small (<6ms) but batch-assembly sometimes 120-250ms for stragglers.

- Fixed-16 / timeout-12 / soft-preempt / proportional:
  p50=25ms p95=62ms p99=136ms p999=310ms
  KV-hit-rate=76%
  notes: p99 improved ~35% vs baseline; throughput slightly lower (~3%) due to smaller batches during steady periods. Fairness (tenant p99 stddev) reduced from 48ms->18ms.

- Adaptive(max64 shrink-to-16) / timeout-30 / preempt-off / small-first:
  p50=20ms p95=54ms p99=182ms p999=540ms
  KV-hit-rate=80%
  notes: good p50/p95, p99 worse than fixed-16; slices grew large during high burst allowing better kernel efficiency but increased wait times for small requests.

- Quantile-target(90%) packing / timeout-12 / hard-preempt / proportional:
  p50=28ms p95=66ms p99=92ms p999=180ms
  KV-hit-rate=70% (down since packing prioritized latency over similar-model grouping)
  notes: best tail reduction but throughput drops ~7% and cache-locality suffers; need to quantify cost/benefit.

Profiling notes (where time goes):
- Assembly time (enqueue->batch-dispatch) is the dominant contributor to p99 in fixed-size policies; we saw 40-85% of p99 in assembly for baseline.
- Kernel queueing + execution accounts for moderate fixed cost; when slices underfilled kernel overhead per-token increases but not enough to explain tail.
- KV-cache misses correlate with high assembly times because cold-KV requests often come from long contexts and need extra pre-processing; combined effect = multiplicative.
- eBPF shows occasional syscalls during slice assembly from snapshotting/metric flush hooks — leads to jitter spikes. Investigate removing blocking syscalls from hot path.

Interpretation / hypotheses:
- Smaller slice sizes + lower timeouts reduce tail by lowering max wait, at the expense of throughput and KV-locality. There is a sweet spot (observed ~16, timeout 12) that meaningfully reduces p99 while keeping throughput within acceptable delta for most workloads.
- Hard preemption with proportional fairness gives best tail for mixed-tenant workloads but penalizes throughput and reduces KV-hit; might be useful as an emergency SLO mode or for high-priority tenants.
- Quantile packing (pack until a targeted latency quantile) is promising for tail but harms cache affinity. Could combine quantile packing + cache-aware grouping (only pack across tenants when cache keys overlap).

Open experiments to run next (prioritized):
1) Combine quantile-target packing with cache-affinity heuristic: pack only requests whose kv-prefix hashes collide (cheap fingerprint). Measure p99 and effective tokens/sec.
2) Instrumented sweep of eBPF-identified syscalls: remove/async metric flush in assembly path and rerun baseline to quantify jitter reduction.
3) Tenant-priority hybrid: enable hard preempt only for top-5% latency-sensitive tenants and measure overall fairness impact.
4) Measure tail under longer-run stability (6 hour runs) to detect drift and warm-start effects on KV caches.

Immediate next steps / runbook for canary (if we pick fixed-16/timeout-12/proportional):
- Create runtime flag: --slice-policy=fixed-size --slice-max=16 --slice-timeout-ms=12 --slice-fairness=proportional.
- Canary rollout plan: 5% traffic for 2h, 10% for 6h, 25% for 12h, observe p99, throttles, error rates.
- SLO checks: if p50 increases >20% or throughput drops >8% compared to baseline, auto-rollback. Also monitor KV-hit-rate delta > -6% as a kill switch.

Questions / unresolved:
- Cost model: how to value throughput loss vs tail improvement? Need product input on acceptable tradeoffs per tier.
- Are there interactions with consolidation scheduler (multi-model co-located batches) that we haven't tested? Likely—schedule separate experiments.
- Is there a cheaper fingerprint for cache-affinity than full key-inspect? We need a microbenchmark for fingerprint false-positive rate.

Notes-to-self / quick commands used in probes:
- export OTEL_ENDPOINT=...; ./run-loadtest --pattern=sinusoid --tenants=10 --duration=3600 --trace-sample=1/50
- grpc trace dump: ./trace-tool aggregate --by=slice-id --hist p50,p95,p99,p999 --out csv
- assembly perf: sudo ./ebpf/assemble_probe --pid <runtime> --out /tmp/assemble-ebpf.log

Draft conclusions (working):
- For immediate reduction of p99 across mixed workloads, fixed-16 + timeout 12ms + proportional fairness looks like the best trade-off we have measured so far.
- Quantile packing + cache-awareness is a strong candidate for further tuning; could be a special mode for latency-first customers.
- Need infra/engineering work to remove blocking syscalls from assembly path before aggressive preemption/packing features—jitter sources magnify tail in weird ways.

Attachments / artifacts (traces & CSVs):
- /artifacts/probe-run/2025-02-25/sinusoid-mixB-fixed16-timeout12.csv
- /artifacts/probe-run/2025-02-25/ebpf-assembly-snapshot.log

TODOs:
- [ ] Run cache-affinity + quantile packing experiment and log results (owner: Marco)
- [ ] Reduce/async metric flush from assembly hot path (owner: Heidi)
- [ ] Prepare canary flag and rollback hooks (owner: Omar)
- [ ] Write short product note asking for throughput vs tail tradeoff guidance (owner: Aisha)

If you pick this up: read the csv traces first (they contain per-tenant histograms) and then re-run the 6h stability run for the chosen candidate.

-- A.P.
